data.description:
Discovered while fixing dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d (potential-powellite-mouflon). Two additional sites raise a bare `WorkflowError`, so error_code_for still maps them to `llm_unavailable` even though neither is an LLM outage:

1. src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:541 — `raise WorkflowError("unknown scripted step {name!r} (not in the step registry)")`. This is a caller/plan-authoring error (an unknown `uses:` step) — arguably `invalid_input`.
2. src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:475 — `raise WorkflowError("the editor front-end bundle is missing ...")`. This is a local build/environment setup condition — neither `invalid_input` nor `not_found` cleanly fit; may warrant a new code or a different mapping.

Both are OUT OF SCOPE for dbca because each needs a NEW error-code design decision (what code should each map to?), which the operator directed to escalate rather than decide inline. The dbca fix deliberately left the bare `WorkflowError` base mapping to `llm_unavailable` to protect execute-time genuine LLM outages (AC3).

Acceptance: decide the correct error code for each site (likely a new WorkflowError subclass per site, mirroring WorkflowNotFoundError), add tests through the actual surfaces proving the code, and keep execute-time outages mapping to llm_unavailable.
data.title: Two more bare WorkflowError sites misclassify as llm_unavailable (executor unknown-step, editor missing-bundle)
